The structure is described in a monoclinic primitive cell with lattice parameters a = 4.8636897 Å, b = 5.14224446 Å, c = 5.880777 Å, α = 90°, β = 90°, and γ = 90.72157092999998°. The input composition comprises one Zr, two Nb, one Zn, and eight O atoms, giving twelve atoms in total. The space group is P2 (number 3), with Hall symbol P 2y, and all atomic positions are given as fractional coordinates.

The supplied coordinates are expressed in the input frame, which is related to the standard frame by q_standard = P q_input + s. The transformation matrix P has rows (0.9999999999999999, 5.0256955545872834×10⁻²⁰, 0.0), (−6.804507102225124×10⁻³³, −4.881593081685453×10⁻³³, −1.0), and (0.0, 1.0, 0.0), with an origin shift s = (0.0, 0.0, 0.75). This near-identity rotation combined with a quarter-cell shift along the c-axis interchanges the b and c axes with a sign change, reflecting a nonstandard setting of the monoclinic cell relative to the conventional P2y orientation.

Within the input cell, the single Zr atom occupies Wyckoff position 1d at fractional coordinates (1/2, 0.671107, 1/2). The two Nb atoms occupy distinct one-fold orbits: Nb at 1a is located at (0, 0.829358, 0), while Nb at 1b is at (0, 0.185909, 1/2). The Zn atom resides at Wyckoff position 1c with coordinates (1/2, 0.30589500000000003, 0).

The eight oxygen atoms are distributed among four independent two-fold orbits of type 2e, each with general coordinate relation (x, y, z). The first oxygen orbit has representative coordinates (0.22326900000000016, 0.887885, 0.6777139999999999). The second is at (0.21281599999999995, 0.10787000000000002, 0.18263399999999996). The third oxygen orbit is represented by (0.2603970000000001, 0.625783, 0.159065), and the fourth by (0.2663159999999999, 0.382328, 0.655335). Each of these 2e positions generates a symmetry-equivalent partner under the twofold rotation operation of the space group, yielding the full complement of eight oxygen atoms in the unit cell.
